item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Sep 30, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Fri Oct 2, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.description:
Arts & Crafts, Community, Gaming, Toddlers, Children, Tweens, Teens
Ever wonder how math can make the impossible look easy? Join us for an interactive, mind-bending session with local mathemagician Doc Yoder!In this workshop, you’ll witness incredible illusions—from predicting secret cards using mathematical patterns to mind-reading feats and surprising card tricks. But we won't just leave you guessing: Doc Yoder will pull back the curtain on "The Mystery Card" to reveal how simple numbers, multiples, and a stacked deck create unforgettable magic.Whether you're a curious beginner, a puzzle enthusiast, or just love a good trick, you’ll leave with hands-on tricks to practice and perform for your friends and family.No advanced math skills required—just bring your curiosity!

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.

item.description:

Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.

item.title: LFS Women’s Gathering — Sat Oct 17, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society **Join us for the first LFS Women's Gathering: Lunch at Loxley's!** This is simply a chance for women in and around LFS to spend some time together — to meet women we may not know well, catch up with women we do, share a meal, talk, laugh, and enjoy one another’s company. There’s no business meeting and no required agenda. We can talk about whatever interests us: our lives, ideas, books, politics, culture, what’s happening in Lancaster, what we’ve been thinking about lately — or anything else that comes up around the table. We’ll also talk a little about whether we’d like to make this a regular gathering and, if so, what **we** would like it to be. For our first get-together, we’re meeting at Loxley’s — an especially fun place to begin, with its Robin Hood and Sherwood Forest theme. And since every good Sherwood Forest gathering needs her: **Maid Marian is welcome at our table.**

item.description:
Music, Everyone
Join us for an evening of Klezmer and Jewish music. Klezmer music is traditional instrumental music of the Ashkenazi Jews. Meet the musicians; Christopher Brooks was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He began studying the violin at PS 8 in Brooklyn Heights and at the Third Street Music School. Attending the New School of Music in Philadelphia, Mr. Brooks studied violin with Jascha Brodsky and Geoffrey Michaels. He has played chamber music and been a member of numerous orchestras. Laurie Haines Reese is a cellist dedicated to creating and performing music—especially new music—that explores the cello’s creative possibilities. An accomplished classical musician with a lifelong curiosity about what else the cello can do, she is equally at home in folk, jazz, improvisatory, and experimental music.
